description.zh-TW: 文昌帝君主管考試與功名，是讀書人最崇敬的神明。
description.en: Wenchang Dijun governs examinations and career success, highly revered by scholars and students.

story.zh-TW: 相傳文昌帝君多次轉世為儒生，累積陰德，最終得道成仙，掌管文運與考試。
story.en: Legend says Wenchang Dijun reincarnated many times as a scholar, accumulating merit before becoming the celestial guardian of literature and exams.

deityStory.zh-TW: 位於台北書院旁，是北部學子祈求考運的聖地，每逢考季香火鼎盛。
deityStory.en: Located near the Taipei Academy, it is a holy site for northern students to pray for exam success, especially busy during exam seasons.

domain.zh-TW: 奪魁、考試第一、金榜題名
domain.en: Coming first in examinations, academic success

description.zh-TW: 魁星爺造型獨特，單足鰲頭，象徵「獨占鰲頭」。
description.en: Kui Xing has a unique appearance, standing on one foot on a giant turtle's head, symbolizing 'coming first in the exam'.

story.zh-TW: 傳說魁星雖有才華但相貌醜陋，考試雖中狀元卻因外貌落選，憤而投江，被鰲魚救起升天。
story.en: Legend says Kui Xing was talented but ugly. Despite passing as the top scholar, he was rejected due to his looks. He tried to drown himself but was saved by a turtle and ascended to heaven.

deityStory.zh-TW: 赤崁樓文昌閣二樓供奉魁星爺，考生常來此祈求金榜題名，並懸掛祈福牌。
deityStory.en: The second floor of the Wenchang Pavilion at Chihkan Tower enshrines Kui Xing, where students often hang prayer cards for academic success.

description.zh-TW: 地基主是住宅的守護神，保佑家宅平安，通常在廚房祭拜。
description.en: Di Ji Zhu is the guardian spirit of the house, ensuring family safety, usually worshipped in the kitchen.

story.zh-TW: 地基主是原本居住在該地的靈魂，入厝或逢年過節需祭拜以示尊重。
story.en: Di Ji Zhu is the original spirit residing on the land. It is worshipped upon moving in or during festivals to show respect.

deityStory.zh-TW: 地基主不供奉於廟宇，而是存在於每個家庭中，是與民眾生活最親近的神祇之一。
deityStory.en: Di Ji Zhu is not enshrined in temples but exists in every household, being one of the deities closest to people's daily lives.

domain.en: Guarding the doors, warding off evil spirits

description.zh-TW: 門神貼於門上，阻擋邪氣進入，最常見的是秦叔寶與尉遲恭。
description.en: Door Gods are pasted on doors to block evil spirits. The most common ones are Qin Shubao and Yuchi Gong.

story.zh-TW: 唐太宗生病夢見惡鬼，秦叔寶與尉遲恭自願夜守宮門，鬼魅不敢侵擾，後遂繪其像貼於門上。
story.en: Emperor Taizong of Tang was haunted by nightmares. Qin Shubao and Yuchi Gong volunteered to guard the palace gates at night. The ghosts ceased, and later their portraits were pasted on doors.

deityStory.zh-TW: 幾乎所有廟宇的大門都繪有門神，是保護廟宇神聖空間的第一道防線。
deityStory.en: Almost all temples have Door Gods painted on their main gates as the first line of defense protecting the sacred space.

description.zh-TW: 七娘媽即織女，是兒童的守護神，十六歲時需行「做十六歲」成年禮。
description.en: Qiniangma is the Weaver Girl, the guardian deity of children. A 'Coming of Age' ritual is performed at age 16.

story.zh-TW: 牛郎織女的故事家喻戶曉，織女七姊妹被視為婦女與兒童的保護神。
story.en: The story of the Cowherd and the Weaver Girl is well-known. The seven weaver sisters are regarded as protectors of women and children.

deityStory.zh-TW: 以舉辦「做十六歲」成年禮聞名，家長會帶子女來此感謝七娘媽庇佑長大成人。
deityStory.en: Famous for the 'Coming of Age' ritual at age 16. Parents bring their children here to thank Qiniangma for protecting them until adulthood.

description.zh-TW: 清水祖師為北宋高僧，神像面容多為黑色，傳說遇災變時鼻子會掉落示警。
description.en: Qingshui Zushi was a high monk in the Northern Song Dynasty. His statue often has a black face. Legend says his nose drops off to warn of impending disasters.

story.zh-TW: 相傳在清水巖修行時，遭山鬼以此火燻燒七日不死，但面目全黑，故稱「烏面祖師」。
story.en: Legend says that while meditating at Qingshui Rock, he was smoked by demons for seven days but survived, turning his face black, hence the name 'Black-Faced Master'.

deityStory.zh-TW: 有「東方藝術殿堂」之美譽，廟宇建築雕刻極為精美，是清水祖師信仰的重鎮。
deityStory.en: Known as the 'Palace of Oriental Art', the temple features exquisite carvings and is a major center for Qingshui Zushi worship.

domain.zh-TW: 守護鄉土、漳州移民守護神
domain.en: Protecting the land, patron deity of Zhangzhou immigrants

description.zh-TW: 開漳聖王本名陳元光，唐代將領，開發漳州有功，被漳州移民視為守護神。
description.en: Kaizhang Shengwang, named Chen Yuanguang, was a Tang general credited with developing Zhangzhou. He is the patron deity of Zhangzhou immigrants.

story.zh-TW: 陳元光平定閩南戰亂，設漳州郡，教化百姓，死後被尊奉為神。
story.en: Chen Yuanguang quelled rebellions in Southern Fujian, established Zhangzhou prefecture, and civilized the people. He was deified after death.

deityStory.zh-TW: 位於內湖山區，視野遼闊，是全台最大的開漳聖王廟之一。
deityStory.en: Located in the Neihu mountains with a wide view, it is one of the largest Kaizhang Shengwang temples in Taiwan.

domain.en: Mountain gods, guardian of Hakka people

description.zh-TW: 三山國王原為廣東潮州的三座山神，隨客家移民來台，成為客家聚落的守護神。
description.en: Sanshan Guowang are originally three mountain gods from Chaozhou, Guangdong. They came to Taiwan with Hakka immigrants and became guardians of Hakka settlements.

story.zh-TW: 傳說三位神人助宋太宗平亂有功，受封為王，分別掌管巾山、明山、獨山。
story.en: Legend says three divine men helped Emperor Taizong of Song quell a rebellion. They were titled Kings, ruling over Jin, Ming, and Du mountains.

deityStory.zh-TW: 竹東地區的信仰中心，主祀三山國王，見證了客家庄的歷史發展。
deityStory.en: The religious center of Zhudong, dedicated to Sanshan Guowang, witnessing the history of the Hakka community.
